propositions: Long-running LLM gate operations (transition, review-plan, verify-completion) emit no output between start and final verdict, causing supervisor stall watchdogs to kill healthy runs that exceed 600s silence windows

A 146.9s gate invocation contained 85.4s silent gap after model-call conclusion; the two dominant silent phases (27s prologue, 40s overlap retrieval) are local compute with no instrumentation at any log level including DEBUG

Closing work is the final step of autonomous runs with maximal accumulated state, so a stall kill on the close path leaves epics and stories stranded in-progress with closed descendants, requiring manual recovery

Supervisor stall budgets (e.g. 600s default) are ordinary and documented as the common case, yet gate ops routinely exceed them while silent, making silent-run tolerance and progress emission incompatible under current design

ADR 0089 defers a stream-event idle watchdog but does not block a periodic liveness heartbeat; existing test suite pins silence-tolerance as correct behavior and constrains any remedy to purely additive emission without total-runtime caps
Documentation deliberately declines to publish expected wall-clock durations for gate operations (per plan-review-gate.md:1420-1424), leaving operators unable to raise supervisor budgets deliberately
